company: First edition, first printing of Bram Stoker's 'Dracula' (1897), seller Bev
product: Pawn Stars clip '$49,000 Price for Rare Dracula Book! | Pawn Stars (S25)' (YouTube id ioFSiIYL6Wc, Pawn Stars official channel, Season 25 Episode 2 'Fangs for the Memories'). Rare books expert Rebecca Romney examines the book, values it at $60,000; Rick offers up to $35,000; seller wants $49,000 (would take $45,000); no deal.

facts.fact: Seller says it is a first edition, first printing of Dracula; Dracula by Bram Stoker, published 1897.
Seller read it many times, fell in love with it and searched a long time for a first edition.
Clamshell box made later, red velvet ('I call it his casket').
Second and third printings had publisher advertisements bound at the back; a true first printing has none - this copy ends on page 390 with a blank and no bookseller ad.
Probably around 3,000 copies of the first printing (not known definitively).
Condition issues: faded lettering, toning to the spine from sun ('the book got sunburned'); Rick jokes about Dracula and sunlight / coffin.
Negotiation: seller $49,000; Rick $30,000; seller $45,000; Rick $35,000 'best I can do'; seller declines; no deal.
facts.source: broadcast transcript ids 109-119; on-screen tags was $49,000 / still $49,000 / now $30,000 / now $45,000 / now $35,000

facts.fact: No confirmed record found of what happened to this copy after the show.
